--- title: "Visualising data with ggplot2" subtitle: "Introduction to Global Health Data Science" date: "2026-08-24" format: revealjs: auto-stretch: false --- ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: ## ggplot2 $\in$ tidyverse :::: {.columns .v-center} ::: {.column width="40%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](../img/ggplot2-part-of-tidyverse.png){fig-align='center' width=80%} ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="60%"} - **ggplot2** is the tidyverse's data visualization package. - The structure of ggplot code can be summarized as: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot( data = my_data, mapping = aes( x = x_var, y = y_var ) ) + geom_xxx() + other_options ``` ::: ::: :::: --- ## Data: Life expectancy from infancy IHME data on location (mostly countries), World Bank region, binary sex, and estimated life expectancy and population in 2023 will be used to explore the men's health gap (later we will add more years). :::: {.columns .v-center} ::: {.column width="30%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](../img/drabernathy.png){fig-align='center' width=50%} ::: ::: *Dr. Abernathy of* **The Simpsons** *(aged 40)* ::: ::: {.column width="70%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} glimpse(lifeexpwide2023) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Rows: 204 Columns: 6 $ location "Afghanistan", "Albania", "Algeria", "A… $ year 2023, 2023, 2023, 2023, 2023, 2023, 202… $ worldbankregion "South Asia", "Europe and Central Asia"… $ pop 38041757, 2854191, 43053054, 55312, 771… $ Female 68.98985, 82.05155, 77.60938, 74.38214,… $ Male 68.13812, 77.27016, 74.54654, 67.96911,… ``` ::: ::: *Grampa Simpson* (Matt Groening) ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](../img/Abraham_Simpson.png){fig-align='center' width=15%} ::: ::: ::: :::: --- ## Life expectancy :::: columns ::: {.column width="70%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w01-02-ggplot_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-7-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="30%"} ### Discuss - What does the color represent? - What overall pattern do you notice? - What additional information would help explain the scatter? ::: :::: --- ## Building the plot ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot( data = lifeexpwide2023, mapping = aes( x = Female, y = Male, color = worldbankregion ) ) + geom_point() + labs( title = "Life expectancy", subtitle = "2023", x = "Female life expectancy", y = "Male life expectancy", color = "World Bank Region" ) ``` ::: --- # Coding out loud --- :::: columns ::: {.column width="60%"}
> **Start with the `lifeexpwide2023` data**
::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot( data = lifeexpwide2023 ) ``` ::: ::: ::: {.column width="40%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w01-02-ggplot_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-10-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: :::: --- ## Coding out loud :::: columns ::: {.column width="60%"}
> Start with the `lifeexpwide2023` data, > **and map female life expectancy to the x-axis**
::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot( data = lifeexpwide2023, mapping = aes( x = Female ) ) ``` ::: ::: ::: {.column width="40%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w01-02-ggplot_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-12-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: :::: --- ## Coding out loud :::: columns ::: {.column width="60%"}
> Start with the `lifeexpwide2023` data, > map female life expectancy to the x-axis, > **and map male life expectancy to the y-axis**
::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot( data = lifeexpwide2023, mapping = aes( x = Female, y = Male ) ) ``` ::: ::: ::: {.column width="40%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w01-02-ggplot_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-14-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: :::: --- ## Coding out loud :::: columns ::: {.column width="60%"}
> Start with the `lifeexpwide2023` data, > map female life expectancy to the x-axis, > map male life expectancy to the y-axis, > **and represent each observation with a point**
::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot( data = lifeexpwide2023, mapping = aes( x = Female, y = Male ) ) + geom_point() ``` ::: ::: ::: {.column width="40%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w01-02-ggplot_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-16-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: :::: --- ## Coding out loud :::: columns ::: {.column width="60%"}
> Start with the `lifeexpwide2023` data, > map female life expectancy to the x-axis, > map male life expectancy to the y-axis, > represent each observation with a point, > **and map region to the color of each point**
::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot( data = lifeexpwide2023, mapping = aes( x = Female, y = Male, color = worldbankregion ) ) + geom_point() ``` ::: ::: ::: {.column width="40%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w01-02-ggplot_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-18-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: :::: --- ## Coding out loud :::: columns ::: {.column width="60%"}
> Start with the `lifeexpwide2023` data, > map female life expectancy to the x-axis, > map male life expectancy to the y-axis, > represent each observation with a point, > map region to the color of each point, > **and title the plot "Life expectancy."**
::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot( data = lifeexpwide2023, mapping = aes( x = Female, y = Male, color = worldbankregion ) ) + geom_point() + labs( title = "Life expectancy" ) ``` ::: ::: ::: {.column width="40%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w01-02-ggplot_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-20-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: :::: --- ## Coding out loud :::: columns ::: {.column width="60%"}
> Start with the `lifeexpwide2023` data, > map female life expectancy to the x-axis, > map male life expectancy to the y-axis, > represent each observation with a point, > map region to the color of each point, > title the plot "Life expectancy," > **and add the subtitle "2023."**
::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot( data = lifeexpwide2023, mapping = aes( x = Female, y = Male, color = worldbankregion ) ) + geom_point() + labs( title = "Life expectancy", subtitle = "2023" ) ``` ::: ::: ::: {.column width="40%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w01-02-ggplot_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-22-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: :::: --- ## Coding out loud :::: columns ::: {.column width="60%"}
> Start with the `lifeexpwide2023` data, map female life expectancy to the x-axis, map male life expectancy to the y-axis, represent each observation with a point, map region to the color of each point, title the plot "Life expectancy," add the subtitle "2023," > **and refine x and y axis labels.**
::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot( data = lifeexpwide2023, mapping = aes( x = Female, y = Male, color = worldbankregion ) ) + geom_point() + labs( title = "Life expectancy", subtitle = "2023", x = "Female life expectancy", y = "Male life expectancy" ) ``` :::
::: ::: {.column width="40%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w01-02-ggplot_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-24-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: :::: --- ## Coding out loud :::: columns ::: {.column width="60%"}
> Start with the `lifeexpwide2023` data, map female life expectancy to the x-axis, map male life expectancy to the y-axis, represent each observation with a point, map region to the color of each point, title the plot "Life expectancy," add the subtitle "2023," refine the axis labels, > **and fix the legend label.**
::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot( data = lifeexpwide2023, mapping = aes( x = Female, y = Male, color = worldbankregion ) ) + geom_point() + labs( title = "Life expectancy", subtitle = "2023", x = "Female life expectancy", y = "Male life expectancy", color="World Bank Region" ) ``` :::
::: ::: {.column width="40%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w01-02-ggplot_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-26-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: :::: --- ## Coding out loud :::: columns ::: {.column width="60%"}
> Start with the `lifeexpwide2023` data, map female life expectancy to the x-axis, map male life expectancy to the y-axis, represent each observation with a point, map region to the color of each point, title the plot "Life expectancy," add the subtitle "2023," refine the axis labels, fix the legend label, > **and add a caption for data source.**
::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot( data = lifeexpwide2023, mapping = aes( x = Female, y = Male, color = worldbankregion ) ) + geom_point() + labs( title = "Life expectancy", subtitle = "2023", x = "Female life expectancy", y = "Male life expectancy", color="World Bank Region", caption = "Source: IHME" ) ``` :::
::: ::: {.column width="40%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w01-02-ggplot_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-28-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: :::: --- ## Argument names ::: {.callout-tip title="Tip"} You can omit the names of the first two arguments when building plots with `ggplot()`. ::: :::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot( data = lifeexpwide2023, mapping = aes( x = Female, y = Male, color = worldbankregion ) ) + geom_point() ``` ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot( lifeexpwide2023, aes( x = Female, y = Male, color = worldbankregion ) ) + geom_point() ``` ::: ::: :::: --- # Aesthetics --- ## Aesthetics options Commonly used characteristics of plotting characters that can be **mapped to a specific variable** in the data are: ::: {.incremental} - `color` - `shape` - `size` - `alpha` (transparency) ::: --- ## Color :::: columns ::: {.column width="40%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot( lifeexpwide2023, aes( x = Female, y = Male, color = worldbankregion ) ) + geom_point() ``` ::: ::: ::: {.column width="60%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w01-02-ggplot_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-32-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: :::: --- ## Shape :::: columns ::: {.column width="40%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot( lifeexpwide2023, aes( x = Female, y = Male, shape = worldbankregion ) ) + geom_point() ``` ::: ::: ::: {.column width="60%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w01-02-ggplot_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-34-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: :::: **Oops!** Only **6** shapes are available, so this isn't a good option for our **more than 6** regions! Let's fix that. --- ## Shape, take 2 :::: columns ::: {.column width="40%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot( lifeexpwide2023, aes( x = Female, y = Male, shape = worldbankregion ) ) + geom_point() + scale_shape_manual(values = c(16,17,15,18,3,4,8,0,1,2)) ``` ::: ::: ::: {.column width="60%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w01-02-ggplot_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-36-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: :::: **Oops!** Only **6** shapes are available, so this isn't a good option for our **more than 6** regions! Let's fix that. --- ## Shape Can also map to the same variable as `color` (helps for color vision deficiency) :::: columns ::: {.column width="40%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot( lifeexpwide2023, aes( x = Female, y = Male, shape = worldbankregion, color=worldbankregion ) ) + geom_point() + scale_shape_manual(values = c(16,17,15,18,3,4,8,0,1,2)) ``` ::: ::: ::: {.column width="60%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w01-02-ggplot_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-38-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: :::: --- ## Size :::: columns ::: {.column width="40%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot( lifeexpwide2023, aes( x = Female, y = Male, color = worldbankregion, size = pop ) ) + geom_point() ``` ::: ::: ::: {.column width="60%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w01-02-ggplot_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-40-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: :::: --- ## Alpha (Transparency) :::: columns ::: {.column width="40%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot( lifeexpwide2023, aes( x = Female, y = Male, color = worldbankregion, alpha = pop ) ) + geom_point() ``` ::: ::: ::: {.column width="60%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w01-02-ggplot_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-42-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: :::: --- ## Mapping vs. setting aesthetics :::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} **Mapping**
::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot( lifeexpwide2023, aes( x = Female, y = Male, size = pop ) ) + geom_point() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w01-02-ggplot_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-43-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: :::
::: ::: {.column width="50%"} **Setting**
::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot( lifeexpwide2023, aes( x = Female, y = Male ) ) + geom_point(size = 2) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w01-02-ggplot_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-44-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: :::
::: :::: --- ## Mapping vs. setting - **Mapping:** Determine the size, alpha, etc. of points based on the values of a variable in the data. - Goes into `aes()`. - **Setting:** Determine the size, alpha, etc. of points **not** based on the values of a variable in the data. - Goes into `geom_*()` (this was `geom_point()` in the previous example, but we'll learn about other geoms soon!). --- # Faceting --- ## Faceting - Smaller plots that display different subsets of the data - Useful for exploring conditional relationships and large data --- ## Faceting :::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} lifeexpwide %>% filter( year %in% c(1999, 2009, 2023), worldbankregion %in% c( "North America", "South Asia", "Sub-Saharan Africa" ) ) %>% ggplot( aes( x = Female, y = Male ) ) + geom_point() + facet_grid(year ~ worldbankregion) ``` ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w01-02-ggplot_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-46-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: :::: --- ## Various ways to facet --- ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} lifeexpwide %>% filter( year %in% c(1999, 2010, 2023), worldbankregion %in% c("North America","South Asia","Sub-Saharan Africa" ) ) %>% ggplot( aes(x = Female, y = Male) ) + geom_point() + facet_wrap(~worldbankregion) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w01-02-ggplot_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-47-1.png){fig-align='center' width=60%} ::: ::: --- ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} lifeexpwide %>% filter(year %in% c(1999, 2010, 2023),worldbankregion %in% c("North America","South Asia","Sub-Saharan Africa")) %>% ggplot(aes(x = Female, y = Male)) + geom_point() + facet_grid(.~worldbankregion) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w01-02-ggplot_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-48-1.png){fig-align='center' width=60%} ::: ::: --- ## Faceting summary - `facet_grid()` - 2D grid - `rows ~ cols` - Use `.` for no split. - `facet_wrap()` - 1D ribbon wrapped according to the number of rows and columns specified or the available plotting area. --- ## Facet and color :::: columns ::: {.column width="60%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} lifeexpwide %>% filter( year %in% c(1999, 2010, 2023), worldbankregion %in% c( "North America", "South Asia", "Sub-Saharan Africa" ) ) %>% ggplot( aes( x = Female, y = Male, color = year ) ) + geom_point() + facet_wrap(~worldbankregion) ``` ::: ::: ::: {.column width="40%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w01-02-ggplot_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-50-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: :::: --- ## Facet and color, no legend :::: columns ::: {.column width="60%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} lifeexpwide %>% filter( year %in% c(1999, 2010, 2023), worldbankregion %in% c( "North America", "South Asia", "Sub-Saharan Africa" ) ) %>% ggplot( aes( x = Female, y = Male, color = year ) ) + geom_point() + facet_wrap(~worldbankregion) + guides(color = "none") ``` ::: ::: ::: {.column width="40%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w01-02-ggplot_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-52-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: ::::

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
